**Answer: 1000**

**Upper bound and block decomposition.** Pair rows and columns as {1,2}, {3,4}, …, {17,18}, {19}. This splits the 19×19 board into 100 blocks: 81 of size 2×2, 9 of size 1×2 (along the bottom), 9 of size 2×1 (along the right), and one 1×1 at (19,19). Every block is a clique in the king-adjacency graph, so each holds at most one selected cell. With 100 blocks and 99 selections, exactly one block is empty and every other block holds exactly one cell.

**Encoding choices.** Give each block a choice (v,h), where v∈{T,B} is top/bottom and h∈{L,R} is left/right. Blocks in the bottom row have v=T forced, and blocks in the right column have h=L forced. The conflicts between occupied blocks are:
- Horizontal: (i,j) has h=R and (i,j+1) has h=L.
- Vertical: (i,j) has v=B and (i+1,j) has v=T.
- Diagonal: (i,j)=(B,R) with (i+1,j+1)=(T,L), or (i,j+1)=(B,L) with (i+1,j)=(T,R).

**Counting for a fixed empty block (p,q).**
- Any row without an empty block forces h=L throughout, since the forced L at the right end admits no "RL" pattern. Likewise any column without an empty block forces v=T throughout.
- In row p, the blocks left of q must have h of the form L…LR…R. That gives q choices.
- In column q, the blocks above p must have v of the form T…TB…B. That gives p choices.
- Blocks to the right of q in row p and below p in column q are forced.
- The only coupling is the diagonal conflict between (p−1,q) with v=B and (p,q−1) with h=R. This removes (p−1)(q−1) of the pq combinations.

So each empty position (p,q) contributes pq − (p−1)(q−1) = p + q − 1 configurations.

**Summing.** Over p,q ∈ {1,…,10}:

Σ(p+q−1) = 2·10·55 − 100 = 1100 − 100 = 1000.

**Check.** The same method on a 3×3 board (2×2 blocks, p,q∈{1,2}) gives 1+2+2+3 = 8, which matches a direct enumeration of 3-cell independent sets.

ANSWER: 1000
